record.summary: Premise false as stated: 'odd-denominator ES is impossible' fails. A sum of unit fractions with all denominators odd and equal to 4/n has an even number of terms (2-adic parity, checked: no 3-term odd solutions for odd n <= 301), but two odd terms already work for 969 of the 1500 odd n in [3,3001] (e.g. 4/3 = 1/1 + 1/3 and 4/9 = 1/3 + 1/9, all denominators odd; the 2-term test is the divisor condition on n^2). So the local 2-adic constraint is a parity-of-count constraint, not an impossibility.

title: Odd-denominator ES is impossible (2-adic): the archetype of a constrained-world local obstruction
connection: If x, y, z are odd, xy + yz + zx is odd and xyz odd, so the reduced fraction has odd numerator, while 4/n (n odd) has numerator 4. So no solution. Likewise exactly one even denominator is impossible by 2-adic valuations (the computation confirms).

avenue.missing_theorem: None for ES. PROVED (elementary): 4/n (n odd) has no solution with all of x, y, z odd, and none with exactly one even. The generalisation to multiplicative sets H ⊂ (ℤ/ℓ^k)^* is a finite local computation (Hensel), and BL's no-BM theorem says the unconstrained local conditions never obstruct.

record.summary: Proof route found and verified exactly for D = 3 (eps = 2+sqrt3, norm +1). eps^5 = 362+209 sqrt3 is -1 mod 11 O_K (11 = 3 mod 4 splits in Q(sqrt3)); kappa = (1+eta)/11 = 33+19 sqrt3 is integral and totally positive (its conjugate is 6/kappa > 0); u = kappa/eta and v = kappa are totally positive and 1/u+1/v = 11, so Lemma 3.1 applies with e = 11. The identity 4/n = 1/x + 1/(u n x) + 1/(v n x), x = (n+11)/4, holds in Q(sqrt3) for n = 5, 9, 13, 17, 21, 101, 1001. This proves positive ES over O_{Q(sqrt3)} for every rational n = 1 mod 4 (EVIDENCE upgraded), and 132 primes l = 3 mod 4 up to 3000 give the same mechanism.

connection: For D = 3, 6, 7 (N(ε) = +1) the rational classes were covered numerically. The proof of Prop 3.3 used N(ε) = −1 to get ε^{ℓ+1} ≡ −1; for N(ε) = +1 one needs another route (e.g. ℓ split and ε of even order modulo a prime above ℓ).

avenue.missing_theorem: For every real quadratic K with N(ε) = +1 and every rational n ≥ 2, positive ES holds over O_K. Route: by Chebotarev pick ℓ ≡ 3 (4) inert in K with the image of ε in the cyclic norm-one group of F_{ℓ²}^* (order ℓ + 1) of even order. Then η = ε^{2j} or ε^j ≡ −1 (mod ℓ) is totally positive, and Lemma 3.1 applies. The Chebotarev condition lives in K(√ε, i) and fails only if ε is a square in K(i)·(…). Some D (e.g. D = 3, ε = 2 + √3 = ((√6+√2)/2)²) need a split-ℓ variant.

record.summary: Lemma 3.1 with eta = l^j (positive units of Z[1/l]) needs only a divisor e = 3 mod 4 of 1+l^j; then kappa = (1+l^j)/e and u = kappa/l^j lie in Z[1/l]_{>0}. For every odd prime l < 400 such an e exists with j <= 12 (j = 1 for l = 5 with e = 3; j = 3 for l = 3 with e = 7; j = 5 for l = 193 and 337 with e = 11). So the Prop 3.2 mechanism covers all odd l < 400, and the |S| = 1 classification is: Z[1/2] (4 a unit, trivial one-term identity) and Z[1/l] for odd l (mechanism applies). Z itself has none.

record.summary: Dirichlet's unit theorem: the unit rank r1 + r2 - 1 is 0 exactly for K = Q and imaginary quadratic K, so those are the unit-rank-0 worlds. The Gaussian cone S = {a in Z[i]: (Re a, Im a) both >= 0 or both <= 0} is not multiplicatively closed: (1+i) and (-1-2i) lie in S but their product 1-3i does not. Lemma 3.1 needs u n x in C, so it does not apply verbatim to the Bradford-Ionascu cone; a Gaussian twin needs a multiplicatively closed cone, and real-place sign conditions do not define one in an imaginary quadratic field.

title: Imaginary quadratic fields are the only other unit-rank-0 worlds: Bradford–Ionascu cone is the right twin
connection: Number fields with finite unit group are Q and imaginary quadratic fields. So among number fields the ES-hard worlds (with a sensible cone) are exactly Q and imaginary quadratics.

avenue.missing_theorem: None for ES. Dirichlet's unit theorem: O_K^× is finite iff K = ℚ or K is imaginary quadratic. So these are the only number-field worlds where the other_rings unit mechanism is absent, and the Bradford–Ionascu Gaussian cone is a natural twin.

record.summary: Pure Ford-circle criterion (BRAINSTORM/farey_ford_cf.md §4): for prime p and b in [1,p), N = b^{-1} mod p and e = (Nb-1)/p, so e/N is the left Farey parent of b/p; the criterion is 4 | N and e | aN+1 for some a | N/4. Over primes 5..3000 it holds for every prime except 5 and 17. The repo's claim that 41 and 241 are also missed is contradicted by explicit witnesses: p = 41 with b = 12, N = 24, e = 7, a = 2 (7 divides 49), and p = 241 with b = 66, N = 84, e = 23, a = 3 (23 divides 253 = 11*23; check 84*66 - 241*23 = 1).

record.summary: Premise: the Galois-orbit equation Tr_{K/Q}(1/x) = 4/p (x ∈ O_K totally positive, K cyclic cubic) is a variant, not a reformulation of ES over Z (x ∈ Z would give 3/x = 4/p); writing Tr(1/x) = s2(x)/N(x) it is p·s2(x) = 4N(x), and for p INERT in K this forces x = p·y with Tr(1/y) = 4, i.e. it is p-independent: solvable for all inert p iff some totally positive z ∈ O_K has Tr(1/z) ∈ 4ℤ_{>0} (PROVED, elementary; x = p(Tr(1/z)/4)z). Search (conductors 7, 9, 13, 19, box |coords| ≤ 60, ~4·10⁵ totally positive x each; also 31, 43, 73 box 40): every prime p ≤ 10⁴ solved is split in K (cond. 7: all split p ≤ 139 hit, no inert or ramified p ever), and NO totally positive z has 4 | Tr(1/z) (integral Tr(1/z) occurs 51–187 times per field with residues 1, 2, 3 mod 4), while without positivity 4 | Tr(1/z) is common (258 cases, cond. 7, box 25) and in non-cyclic totally real cubics m = Tr(1/z) ≡ 0 (4) is abundant (34 768 polys for m = 4, a ≤ 120) but cyclic (square disc) has 0 for m = 4, 8, 12, 16 vs 2–31 for every other m ≤ 16 (EVIDENCE). CONJECTURE: a positivity-dependent, cyclic-specific obstruction 4 ∤ Tr(1/z) (in fact Tr(z)·Tr(1/z) ≢ 0 (mod 4) in all 75 cyclic hits) blocks every inert prime; PROVED for units when 2 is inert and totally positive units are squares (F₈ trace argument: Tr(w̄) = Tr(w̄⁻¹) = 0 impossible).
record.not_done: No proof of the mod-4 obstruction for non-units (2-adic discriminant analysis shows it is not a 2-adic condition on D alone: D ≡ 1 mod 8 is possible; Hilbert-symbol/trace-form route not completed); split primes beyond the box (p > ~300) not solved, so 'all split p solvable' is untested beyond ~139; only Z[θ] (index 2/3 orders) for conductors 31, 43, 73.
record.next: Try to prove 4 ∤ Tr(1/z) for totally positive z in cyclic cubic fields via am − 9 = Tr((z−σz)²/(zσz)) (u totally positive, N(u) = (Δ/c)²) or a Hasse-invariant computation of Tr(y v²); it would be a clean positivity+reciprocity obstruction of the type ES lacks (Bright–Loughran).

title: Positive ES over O_K for n ∈ O_K with Galois-conjugate denominators only
connection: Require the three denominators to form a Galois orbit (K cubic, x, σx, σ²x): 4/n = Tr(1/x). Then ES becomes 'n/4 is the reciprocal of a trace of a reciprocal' — a norm-form equation.

avenue.role: norm-form reformulation in a cubic field: 4/p = Tr_{K/ℚ}(1/x)
avenue.missing_theorem: None for ES: the denominators x, σx, σ²x are not rational integers, so a solution is not an ES solution. As a Diophantine statement, 4N(x) = p·Tr(σx·σ²x) is a ternary cubic equation in the coordinates of x, and K has unit rank 2, so the other_rings unit mechanism is available there. ES over ℤ would need x ∈ ℤ, giving 3/x.
avenue.status_ref: BRAINSTORM/other_rings.md §4 (unit rank ≥ 1 collapses positive ES; no transfer to ℤ)
avenue.note: The Thue/Schmidt angle needs the equation over ℤ, and the Galois-orbit constraint takes it out of ℤ.

record.summary: Did the parity test at fixed sieve data (same programs as Z3072): write N_C = s·r with s the N^{1/3}-smooth part, r the rough part (Ω(r) ≤ 2). PROVED (elementary): N ≡ 1 (mod 4C) forces r ≡ s⁻¹, so when Ω(r) ≤ 1 success at C is a function of (s, C) alone; the only sieve-invisible information is the split r = r₁r₂ (Ω(r)=2) — exactly Selberg's parity datum. EVIDENCE: at the same τ(s)- and C-stratum, Ω(r)=2 raises success 1.8–6× over Ω(r)=1 (e.g. τ(s)=2, C∈[10,100): 0.0058 vs 0.036), the Liouville marginal is blind (P = 0.00022 vs 0.00022 at 10⁹), and 82–86 % of certificates are decided by s (10⁶ full ranges: 80.7 %, 10⁷: 82.1 %); but p = 1044877 (≡ 757 mod 840) has R(p) > 0 with all 5 certificate levels (C = 1, 3, 68, 3958, 130610) parity-invisible, 1 of 3642 primes in [10⁶,1.1·10⁶] (0 of 282 near 10⁷, min 4 visible levels). So a sieve/parity-blind argument at level N^{1/3} cannot certify every prime, although parity affects only ≈ 1/5 of certificates on average (Assessment); the odd-square (T1) obstruction is not of parity type (it has identical 1-dimensional sieve densities over C, ρ(ℓ)=1 for ℓ ∤ 2m, and kills all Ω).
record.not_done: 'Visible' is defined only for the cut z = N^{1/3} (no scan over z); no literature theorem (Friedlander–Iwaniec Opera de Cribro ch. 16 parity) was read beyond the standard statement; frequency of zero-visible primes above 10⁶ not estimated (only 282 primes at 10⁷).
record.next: Scan the cut z = N^θ and count zero-visible primes in [10⁶,10⁷] to see whether parity-invisible primes thin out.

title: Parity problem in sieve theory
connection: Sieve parity problems share F21, F22, F40 and explain why robust average estimates may fail to detect a single required arithmetic type.

avenue.role: parity problem in sieve theory as ES's obstruction
avenue.missing_theorem: (Answered, negative.) Slice success does not depend on λ(4Cp+1) (0.051 vs 0.052; out_Q07 Z1996). Prime N_C (Ω = 1) always fails, and success grows with Ω. ES's obstruction is the tied divisor class (B2), not parity. Parity-breaking at fixed p collapses into H-A ((J)6, (J)87).

record.summary: Audited paper/es-threequarter-note.tex: the ONLY ineffective input is Bombieri–Vinogradov (eq. BV, R=26) in the lower bound of Thm supply, over moduli q=4uv ∈ (4X^{1/24}, 4x^{1/3}]; BT, Shiu, lattice sums, moments, void and ledger are effective. BMOR (arXiv:1802.00085, Thm 1.1/1.2 verified: valid only for x ≥ exp(0.03√q log³q) when q>10⁵) cannot replace it — the range is never met for q ≥ X^{1/24}, and pointwise x/(φ(q)log x) bounds summed over q are structurally too weak; Platt–Trudgian is irrelevant here. Assessment (proof sketch): an effective BV off one Landau–Page modulus r1 (Akbary–Hambrook Thm 1.2, explicit c0=48.83, for conductors > (log x)^31; effective zero-free region below) plus BMOR Prop 1.11 (β ≤ 1−40/(√q log²q)) for r1 ≤ (log x)^{1.9}, and dropping the triples with r1 | 4uv (relative mass loss ≪ (log x)^{−1.9+ε}) otherwise, makes c_*, C_* of the 3/4 theorem effective. Premise of `why` fails: N·exp(−c(log N)^{3/4}) → ∞, so no effective/explicit version can ever certify 'no counterexample below X' (data/z52b/pass2/ZF1/Z2418/effectivity.md §5).
record.not_done: No rewrite of the note; Shiu constant not made explicit (so 'effective', not 'explicit'); log log and m/n notes only grepped, not re-derived; sketch not independently reviewed.
record.next: Insert an 'effective BV off the exceptional modulus' lemma into the 3/4 note and have it reviewed, changing 'ineffective' to 'effective' in Thm 1.1.

record.summary: Exponent-covering search for I3 (n = tuv−u−v, t,u,v ≥ 3) with all two-fixed-coordinate words (E: uv | n+u+v; L: (tu−1) | n+u), moduli ≤ 3000–12000 incl. those sharing primes with the base (scripts/z52d_p2_ZF1_Z2776_i3cover.py; positive controls 2^k±1, 3·2^k+1 reproduce I3_DEEP_FABLE Thm 5.5). PROVED (computer-assisted): I3(3^k+2) ≥ 1 for all k ≥ 3, k ≠ 4, by three L-words of period 12 [(3,3), (4,4), (13,7)]; also 5·3^k−1 and 2·3^k+1 close (L = 12). for k ≥ 14 (checked by direct division to k = 400, smaller k by brute force) 3^k−2 is covered except k ≡ 1 (mod 240) (small zeros k = 2, 3), 5·3^k+1 except k ≡ 1, 2 (mod 48), 3^k−1 except k ≡ 1 (mod 48); the residual limit points equal tiny I3 zeros (1, 16, 46, 2, …) away from 3 and lie in no word class of modulus ≤ 3·10⁶, and for 3^k−2 I PROVED (root-splitting mod prime powers) that the point (1 at p≠3, −2 at 3) lies in no E- or L-class at all, so no fixed-word exponent covering of 3^k−2 exists (md_S6.md §Z2776).
record.not_done: No moving-word (window) search for the residual classes; sterility proofs for the points of 3^k−1, 5·3^k+1, 3^k+1 not written (EVIDENCE only); 5^k±1 only at B = 3000; the 3^k+2 proof is not formalised in Lean and has no independent second checker beyond direct division for k ≤ 400.
record.next: Search moving words for n = 3X²−2, X = 3^j (the I3 analogue of the Sophie-Germain window) on the residual class k ≡ 1.

title: I3 at 2^k ± 1 by exponent coverings: Sierpiński-number technique
connection: I3 holds on 2^k ± 1 etc. by exponent coverings (I3_DEEP). This is exactly the Sierpiński/Riesel-number covering technique for k·2^n + 1 compositeness.

avenue.role: thin-family coverage of I3 by exponent coverings (Sierpiński technique)
avenue.missing_theorem: I3 (n = tuv − u − v, t, u, v ≥ 3) holds for every n = 3^k ± 2 and every n = 5·3^k + 1, via a finite covering of the exponent k by congruence classes, each class with an algebraic factorisation or a fixed small witness. Plausible: the same technique closed 2^k ± 1, 2^k ± 3, 7·2^k − 1, 5·2^k − 1 and 3·2^k + 1 (I3_DEEP).
avenue.yield: partial (thin families for I3; no transfer to primes, FRONTIER §1, §4 line 16)
avenue.status_ref: FRONTIER §7.17 (I3 on 2^k ± 1 etc. by exponent coverings, I3_DEEP_ASTRA/FABLE); BRAINSTORM/bsE_sierpinski_moving_integer.md
avenue.next: Run the I3_DEEP exponent-covering harness on 3^k ± 2 (base 3: covering moduli dividing ord_ℓ(3)) for k ≤ 200 and see whether a finite covering closes.
avenue.note: Plausibility 3 refers to the thin-family statement, not ES.

record.summary: Complete searches (scripts/z52_bank_pencil.c, odd n ≤ 5·10⁴): non-square fibres have only sporadic zeros (k=2: 13 zeros, k=3: only n=13, k=5: 21, 57, k=6: none, k=7: 9 zeros ≤ 10⁴, none in (10⁴, 5·10⁴)), against 1262/1250/417 zeros at square controls k=1/4/9 for odd n < 10⁴. The unique k=3 zero n=13 is the unique point on the Mordell locus 4k+n³=□ (13³+12=47²), where Z52_BANKED §1(a) says 𝒜=(−q,−d) is unramified; all 133 901 integral-place local symbols at (13,3) are +1. New Theorem 1(b) (PROVED here, Hilbert reciprocity via dd′=(ny+2k/n)²−k(s/n)²): if k=(s²−n³)/4 ≥ 1, gcd(n,k)=1 and (−n/ℓ)=1 for all ℓ | s, ℓ ∤ k, then S_{n,k}(ℕ)=∅. CERTIFIED on 55 861 Mordell pairs (n ≤ 3001, k ≤ 10⁶): 13 682/13 682 empty; with gcd=1 but a bad prime ℓ | s, (−n/ℓ)=−1, 57 % (17 829/31 548) are still empty vs 2.5 % (298/11 986) for adjacent non-Mordell controls. Assessment: the pencil obstruction lives on {k=□} ∪ {4k+n³=□}; for fixed non-square k the second set is finite (Siegel), and at k=0 it is exactly the odd squares, so T1 is the k→0 limit of the Mordell-locus obstruction (data/z52b/pass2/ZF1/parts/md_S4.md §Z2835).
record.not_done: Full Br S_{n,k}/Br ℚ not computed (no other classes searched for at the sporadic zeros, e.g. k=2, n=3465); the 57 % residual emptiness on bad-prime Mordell fibres is not explained (a quantitative strong-approximation effect is suspected); Thm 1(b) has had no independent review.
record.next: Independent review of Thm 1(b); then test whether the residual Mordell-fibre emptiness is a BM obstruction to strong approximation (solutions need a bad ℓ | d with y ≡ −2k/n² mod ℓ).

title: Goldfeld–Gross–Zagier-type effectivity: an auxiliary L-function with a high-order zero
connection: Goldfeld showed that an L-function with a zero of order ≥ 3 at s = 1/2 makes Siegel effective (Gross–Zagier supplied it). For an ineffective ES theorem (via Siegel), an analogous auxiliary object with a forced high-order vanishing would make p₀ explicit.

avenue.role: effectivisation step: make an (as yet non-existent) Siegel-ineffective ES threshold explicit via a Goldfeld–Gross–Zagier-type auxiliary L-function with a high-order zero
avenue.missing_theorem: Conditional template: if 'ES(p) for all p > p₀' were proved with p₀ depending ineffectively on a possible Siegel zero, an auxiliary L-function with a forced zero of order ≥ 3 at s = 1/2 (GZ) would make p₀ explicit.
avenue.yield: none until an ineffective ES theorem exists; then 'ES for all n' via finite check
avenue.status_ref: No ES step currently depends on Siegel (Z2931: the BM main term is effective; BM_LVALUE Thm A effective). Goldfeld's theorem gives h(−d) ≫ log d/log log d-type effective bounds, far below Siegel's d^{1/2−ε}, so it only rescues steps that need a very weak L(1,χ) lower bound.
avenue.barrier: premise absent (no ineffective ES theorem); B2 upstream
avenue.next: None now; if a Siegel step ever appears, check whether L(1,χ) ≫ (log q)/q^{1/2}-type (Goldfeld) is enough there.
